title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel eaten, with added fat, NS as fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a product obtained by cooking fresh tubers in salted water. The peel is left on, increasing dietary fiber content. A small amount of vegetable fat (type NS – non‑specific) is added to the dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is the fourth most produced food crop worldwide.
The edible peel contains almost twice the fiber of the flesh.
Boiling preserves most of the vitamin C if not overcooked.
Adding a little fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and D.
Potatoes can be stored at +4 °C for several months.

items.title: Rich in carbohydrates
items.content: Provides complex carbs that supply steady energy without rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Supports immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Fiber in the peel
items.content: Aids digestive health and helps lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Regulates fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Fat enhances vitamin bioavailability
items.content: Vegetable fat helps the body absorb vitamins A and D more efficiently.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to potato.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt should be considered, especially for individuals with hypertension.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes have a high GI, which can raise blood sugar quickly.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Prolonged boiling can produce small amounts of acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish, dice into salads, mash, or bake with vegetables. Rinse the peel well before boiling. Add 1‑2 tsp of vegetable oil to improve flavor and vitamin absorption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep boiled potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Longer storage may lead to soft texture and loss of flavor.
